title: Rectangular base
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. This sketch consists of a single loop made up of four straight lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and extends to (0.75, 0.1034). The third line runs from (0.75, 0.1034) back to (0.0, 0.1034), and the fourth line completes the loop by returning to the origin. After drawing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to reduce its size proportionally. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector of zeros. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.017 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The resulting dimensions of the rectangular base are 0.75 units in length, 0.1034 units in width, and 0.017 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1034) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1034) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.017)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1034, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1034, 0.017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
